01 / VISUAL DIRECTION

Confident. Connected. Human.

Deep navy creates the foundation. Electric blue and cyan express intelligence and possibility; burgundy gives the workshop and secondary moments warmth. Pale blue sections create a calm reading rhythm. Space Grotesk headlines and Manrope body copy are locally hosted in this concept.

Use the original transparent Bluzee logo, with white lettering and a bright red U on navy, and navy lettering with the same red U on pale blue. Do not place it in a white box. Illustrative imagery supports offerings; only original sourced media represents actual sessions or testimonials.

Motion and accessibility

Calm people-centred homepage motion, moving capability typography, cinematic Vision and Mission chapters, staggered reveals, and gentle pointer-driven image depth. A reading-progress line responds to scrolling. Native scroll, no scroll hijacking, no autoplay audio or video. Respect reduced-motion preferences and expose a persistent motion control. Use visible focus, real headings, keyboard-operable menus, accessible tabs and labelled forms.

04 / Offering page layouts

Each page includes a distinctive headline, concise value proposition, relevant visual, next-step CTA and the matching PDF where supplied. Follow with business value, four capabilities, offering-specific detail, practical steps, scope qualifications and related offerings. Dimaq™ and DealTailor™ have interactive illustrative workflows; support has eight checklist accordions; the AI Hub has separate stream curricula, a comparison table, shared evidence, industries and career pathways.

05 / Wix implementation

  1. Build privately. Confirm whether the current site uses Wix Editor or Wix Studio. Wix now supports an unpublished Studio version for eligible Premium Editor sites. The old design does not transfer; some dashboard/app data is shared. Keep live content and media untouched. A standalone Wix duplicate is an alternative.
  2. Use native layouts. Recreate sections with Studio grids, stacks and responsive constraints. Recommended design breakpoints: desktop 1001px+, tablet 751–1000px, mobile 320–750px. Use normal page scrolling and a collapsed mobile menu.
  3. Model content. Use an Offerings CMS collection with slug, category, title, summary, image, capabilities, process, scope and PDF document fields. Use a separate Proof collection for type, title, institution, original source URL, video/media ID, poster, attribution and consent status. Detailed flagship pages may remain static; services can use a dynamic page template with variant sections.
  4. Navigation and PDFs. Use native menu items in a three-level dropdown or accessible mega menu. Link a regular button to the CMS Document field for brochure downloads; Wix’s dedicated Document Button cannot currently bind directly to collections.
  5. Media preservation. Retain existing Wix Video IDs and original student players. Use original posters, click-to-play, controls and source links. Do not recreate testimonial quotations or substitute generated event imagery.
  6. Forms. Replace this concept’s email-draft form with Wix Forms, configured recipients, spam protection, consent wording and a real confirmation after successful submission. No CRM connection or submission has been set up in this concept.
  7. Motion. Use native entrance and hover effects where possible. Match the reduced-motion behaviour and avoid stacked heavy effects. The interactive workflow tabs can be native multi-state boxes; Velo is optional for filters or more complex state. No third-party animation library is necessary.
  8. Launch separately. Review in Wix Preview / Get Client Feedback, test at agreed breakpoints, approve redirect and legal mappings, verify every download and recording, and only publish after a separate launch decision. A Studio plan may be required for launch; publishing the Studio version prevents republishing the original Editor version.

Dynamic homepage & media destinations

The latest direction uses a calm, people-centred collaboration scene, modular ERP architecture, a cursor-responsive digital field guide and an illustrative project-delivery scene.
